Definition: from G5483; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty:--(free) gift.
BiblicalUsage: Charisma is a free gift of grace, and Paul uses it for both the gifts of the Spirit and the gift of salvation itself. There are diversities of gifts but the same Spirit, to another faith and to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit. The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. Peter says every man should minister the gift he has received, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word will not let me earn what God gives: a gift is a gift, whether it is healing or eternal life. Paul puts the Spirit's gifts and salvation under the same word on purpose. I hold that the right response to a gift is stewardship, and Peter says so plainly: minister it to one another.
